# Boylston SwissSys fixtures (pseudonymized)

Seven real US Chess rating-report packages (2C format: `THEXPORT.DBF`,
`TSEXPORT.DBF`, `TDEXPORT.DBF`) written by SwissSys for club events in 2026
and uploaded to US Chess MUIR, which **accepted all of them**. They are the
empirical baseline for what the US Chess importer tolerates (see
`scripts/mock_uscf_importer.py`).

Generated by:

    python3 scripts/anonymize_boylston.py SOURCE_DIR USCF_JSON test/fixtures/boylston

## What was changed

Each DBF is byte-identical to what SwissSys wrote except for these cells
(same width, space-padded):

- Every US Chess member ID (`D_MEM_ID`, `H_CTD_ID`, `H_ATD_ID`, `H_OTHER_TD`,
  `S_CTD_ID`, `S_ATD_ID`) is replaced by a synthetic `9xxxxxxx` ID. One mapping
  covers all events, so a person in several events or sections keeps one ID.
- `D_NAME` is replaced by a synthetic name with the same format quirks as the
  original (case style, `LAST,FIRST` vs `Last, First` vs `First Last`, a TAB
  after the comma, multi-word surnames, middle names).
- `H_AFF_ID` is `A9999999`.

Everything else is kept as written: header garbage bytes, the `26` year byte,
all-`C` descriptors (including the date fields), blank event IDs, blank
`S_SCH_LVL`/`S_GP_PTS`/`D_STATE`, loose time-control spellings, ratings,
SwissSys double-game codes (`$ # % W D L`), forfeit codes without opponents,
and `U0` padding. Event names, dates, and locations are real, so treat this
data as pseudonymized, not anonymous. Do not add real names or IDs here.

## `uscf.json`

The US Chess public rated record for the event: what MUIR actually rated,
reduced to section metadata, per-player `score` and round outcomes, and
officials. It uses the same synthetic ID mapping, and all names are dropped.

This record includes any edits the TD made in the US Chess portal after the
upload, so it can differ from the DBFs. Known cases:

- `may-ladder` section 1 (double games): the rated rounds and scores differ
  heavily from the DBF.
- `april-ladder` section 2: one player's member ID was corrected, and a
  forfeit (`X0`) was given an opponent.
- `springfestival` section 3 (side game): rated with 5 rounds, but the DBF has 1.
- `springfestival` section 1: unmatched `X0`/`Z0` cells were rated as a
  forfeit pairing, a full bye, and a half-point bye.

Double-game rounds (`S_TRN_TYPE` `2`, or SwissSys `$ # %` codes) were rated as
two rounds each.
